# Release and operations plan

The complete plan covers the whole product. A specific release enables only capabilities with proven source support and accepted evidence; disabled capabilities are explicit, never zero-filled.

Creating this repository, issue hierarchy and Project establishes the delivery plan. It does not install a GitHub App, select a host, provision credentials, enable a public metric or deploy a website. Staging validation and production verification remain separate work packages.

## Release phases

**Phase:** Concept and Project publication

**Exit:** Approved concept, issue hierarchy, preserved existing scope and recorded open decisions

**Not claimed:** Implementation, data accuracy or deployment

**Phase:** Synthetic design prototype

**Exit:** Representative accessible journeys and all failure states reviewed using labeled synthetic data

**Not claimed:** Live contributor counts

**Phase:** Public-data shadow collection

**Exit:** Read-only sources, replay, reconciliation and source-specific coverage verified; no public rankings

**Not claimed:** Complete historical observability

**Phase:** Public beta

**Exit:** Working public journeys, attribution/LOC/triage audits, functional correction controls, disclosed limitations and active operator

**Not claimed:** Unsupported qualitative recognition or guaranteed service targets

**Phase:** Production launch

**Exit:** Prelaunch staging acceptance, explicit release authority, deployed revision readback, fresh source progress, accessibility/privacy/recovery receipts

**Not claimed:** Completion of every optional expansion

**Phase:** Full project acceptance

**Exit:** Every in-scope work package completed or explicitly descoped by owner with reason; enabled-capability manifest reconciled; operations handed off

**Not claimed:** Future scope implicitly implemented

## Operational readiness

Agree hosting, cost ceilings, separate staging and production environments, database lifecycle, secret rotation, backup retention, restore ownership, alerts and incident response. Measure ingestion delay, queue depth, retry/dead-letter counts, reconciliation gaps, source permission failures, projection freshness and public error rates. Redact sensitive details from public health surfaces.

Exercise restart, replay, rollback, migration failure, missing webhook recovery, source removal and restoration from backup. A restore test includes recomputation and an independently checked public snapshot. Dashboards, runbooks and alert destinations require accepted operators; a configured endpoint alone does not establish an operating commitment.

Publish an explicit degraded mode. Serve a known safe snapshot with a stale indicator when collection is delayed; suppress data when privacy or scope is uncertain. Rebuilding and disconnected states must be visible on the public site and live wall.

## Production readback

**Owner package:** LB-20.04

### Checks

- Approved DNS/TLS and public URL
- Expected artifact and snapshot revision
- Anonymous board/profile/evidence journey
- Fresh webhook or reconciliation update observed
- Stale indicator and rollback procedure verified
- Actual correction submission receipt
- Operator acknowledgment

A release is complete only with the accepted deployment decision, real public URL, expected revision and independent anonymous readback. Report observed behavior and remaining limits. Never call a rendered form delivered without a verified submission receipt.
